title: StoryPins
pitch: Neighborhood stories, told by the people who live here.
recommendation: Start with a consent-based listening pilot in one neighborhood.
mvp: Five resident-approved recordings, editable transcripts, approximate map pins and a clear removal request process.
needs: A neighborhood host and oral-history adviser
Recording space, microphones and accessibility testing
funding: Connecting California is a plausible future match for public storytelling events with an eligible host. The published rounds are closed; no funding is committed.
test: Can five residents record, review and choose what to share? Can another resident find a story without exposing a private address?
risks: Obtain specific recording/publication permission, offer pseudonyms and coarse locations, separate public media permission from the code license, and make withdrawal practical.

title: ReadySac
pitch: Practice a few decisions before an emergency.
recommendation: Build a five-minute, clearly labeled preparedness exercise using local official guidance.
mvp: One heat/smoke scenario with branching choices, explanation of each choice and a checklist linking to SacAlert and official zone maps.
needs: A preparedness educator to review every scenario
A library or community venue for a small facilitated test
funding: SMUD Shine and future resilience coalitions are partner-led prospects. Current listed rounds are closed and a standalone app is not sufficient eligibility.
test: Can families explain their next preparedness step after the exercise? Check source dates and ensure no simulated message resembles a live warning.
risks: Never predict evacuation decisions or replace official alerts. Avoid competitive scoring that shames people with fewer resources; offer accessible and low-cost choices.

title: Heat & Smoke Check-In
pitch: Help neighbors understand conditions and coordinate a simple check-in.
recommendation: Pilot an opt-in buddy check-in with official condition links and visible timestamps.
mvp: A condition summary, a voluntary “I’m okay / please check in” interaction, and links to verified local resources. Use simulated check-ins until a real coordinator is assigned.
needs: A community organization responsible for follow-up
Multilingual outreach and accessible message design
funding: Seek in-kind coordination and venue support first. SMUD and resilience-center funding may support a broader eligible program in a future cycle.
test: Test stale-data handling and what happens when nobody responds. Agree on a real response protocol before recruiting vulnerable residents.
risks: A check-in is not emergency monitoring. Collect no diagnoses or precise home locations in the public board. Never promise response times without staffed coverage.

title: SMS Resource Finder
pitch: Make verified local help easier to find from a basic phone.
recommendation: Validate referral usefulness with 211 and a small permissioned directory before paying for live SMS.
mvp: A web-based SMS-style conversation over 10 manually verified resources, with language choice, source dates and an easy human-referral exit.
needs: A referral partner and named directory steward
A permitted data feed and a budget for messaging
funding: Nonprofit community-service support or a sponsored pilot is more credible than a grant for a generic chatbot. Verify each fund’s geography and applicant requirements.
test: Measure correct referrals and dead ends with sample requests. Test outdated hours, no matches and urgent needs; do not infer eligibility.
risks: Never scrape a directory on the assumption it is open data. Live SMS has consent, opt-out, carrier registration and per-message costs that require separate setup.
